title: Fig and the Fuss
checkpoint: Reception Autumn 2, week 3 — Learning — Phase 2: new sounds l, ll, ss
note_for_grown_ups: The first book where every recurring cast member's name is fully decodable except Olive's (her name needs the 'v' sound, taught in Learning — Phase 3) — she's still allowed to appear by name, same as any real reading scheme lets its cast keep their names throughout.

pages.illustration: Wide establishing view of the whole garden at sunrise — vegetable patch, pond, log, oak — with the sun just clearing the fence. Bright and hopeful. Set the world up here, since this is the first book with the full cast.

pages.text: Fig digs. Ned digs. Fig and Ned dig a lot.
pages.illustration: Fig the green striped caterpillar and Ned the gold duckling digging side by side in the soft earth of the vegetable patch, soil flying, both entirely covered in it. Fig is doing it carefully; Ned is not.

pages.text: Nell hums off to the log.
pages.illustration: Nell the sunflower-yellow bee flying in a wobbly line towards a mossy log, motion shown by the curve of her path and a few loose petals in her wake.
Moss the hedgehog fast asleep on his back in a warm patch of sun, spikes flat, one leg twitching. Utterly relaxed. Warm gold and berry tones.

pages.text: Ned has a fuss. Ned huffs and puffs.
pages.illustration: Ned mid-tantrum: wings out, beak wide, feathers puffed, standing in the dug-up soil. Draw him bigger than the others on the page so the fuss feels enormous.

pages.text: No fuss, Ned. Go to Fig.
pages.illustration: Fig at the edge of the frame holding out one small leg towards Ned, calm and patient. Ned still cross but half-turned towards him. Two colours, lots of space, the emotional turn of the book.

pages.text: Ned sits. Ned is not sad.
pages.illustration: Ned sitting quietly beside Fig on the log, still muddy, now smiling. Their shoulders touching. Small, warm and close-cropped.

pages.text: Fig, Ned, Nell and Moss sit in the sun.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the whole cast sitting together at the edge of the pond in the morning sun, water like glass, everyone facing the sun. Calm and warm.
